answer: A bond of 15% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in lagoon, and voyage reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 150 aliases, and each one needs its own funded beacon account. That bill is paid per identity, so 310 aliases cost 32 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
